Abstract

Five essays in, a value-content's whole history is on the table, and so is what happens when two of them collide. All five were about one person's own side.

One spine runs through this one, and it is two sentences. The other's value is not my value. That the other can have values of his own, and that this is not mine to give, is my value. They are not two things side by side: the second takes the first as its object. What I avow is precisely the thing the first sentence states. Can have says he can have them without waiting on me. I do not permit him to have them, and I have no place from which to permit it. This is a first-person sentence, said by a bearer who has already avowed it; this essay does not assert that every bearer says it.

Around the spine are three limits. For one particular other, third-person evidence does not close into a reading guaranteed to be complete. Between two bearers, their contents' value-standings take no common external ruler. Among many, relational crossing, resonance, joint decision and joint arrangement are not by themselves enough to merge existing sources into one.

What most needs guarding against is not saying too little. It is reading the three limits into one sentence: then everyone lives their own life. Written short — cannot be read through, cannot be compared, cannot be merged — a reader will draw that on his own. The inference fails, and the reason is not that the reader missed something. It is that the limits do not entail it. A limit says which operations I do not have on another's values. It does not say there is no relation between him and me.

1. The Friend Who Fixed the Window

A man has a friend he has known for years. He knows some of what the friend cares about: getting the window of the old house fixed, going once a year to that river, not letting anyone else take over the work in his hands. He can see all of it, and none of it is his doing. If some day the friend sets one of them down, that is the friend setting it down.

That the friend cares about them mostly has a provenance. His father taught him; something happened one year that changed his mind; he read a certain book early. Those provenances are all there, and none of them is the friend's own making. What makes fixing the window the thing he cherishes is his claiming of it. Cultivation loosening a grid, occupation seizing the site of occurrence — both are on the side of conditions. They can move what he is able to come across. They cannot move that claiming. Constitution is not made on the side of conditions.

So there are two things, and the order cannot be reversed. First, a fact: this particular friend is also an end, and that holds before I acknowledge it. Second, a response: acknowledging and taking up that fact from the first-person place. What acknowledgment does is acknowledge the fact and take it up. It does not make the fact.

A bearer unfolded to 15DD has, in its own law, an outward-facing content: acknowledging a particular other as an end. That was established earlier, along with the note that this content of the law and that row of source are two faces of one place — not a layer added on top of the source — and that no lateral obligation follows from it.

What this essay picks up is a further step. Inside that outward content there is one specific thing: the other can have values of his own, and this is not mine to give. When does it stop being merely a content of the law at that layer and become an avowed value-content under this bearer's name? The line is exactly that claiming.

2. When It Becomes Mine

It holds in three parts. That the other can have values of his own and that this is not mine to give is a fact prior to me. Whether I avow it is a first-person occurrence on my side. Not avowing does not change the first sentence, and avowing does not create it. So it is not something every bearer has by nature — and someone who has not avowed it does not thereby make the fact untrue.

It is inferred, in this order. The other is an end — that is the premise. I am an end, and the first-person source of value is here in me. The other falls in the same place of being an end, so that source is likewise in him, and he can likewise have values of his own. Likewise in the place, not likewise in the content: he has his own share, not a share the same as mine.

There is no observation on this chain. Even if I can read nothing at all of what that friend cares about, the conclusion stands. The converse does not: one may not say because I see he has values of his own, he is an end. A place where something bears is not a place where it is grounded.

A baby who cannot yet say what he wants has a source of value likewise not mine to give. In that sentence he counts as the other. As the party doing the avowing he does not yet count; the 15DD row is not yet actually running inside him.

The 15DD value-source is the irreplaceability of the other as an end. That is a noun — the shape in which this row can yield candidates. What this section speaks of is an avowed content on that row, the thing that fits into the shape. The shape is not the content.

Once avowed, this content takes the same value-standing as any other avowed content under that person's name. It is not on another layer, and it is not a value about values. In a concrete situation it can organize demands for action, and it can collide with another content, and then it settles by the adjudication established in the previous essay. What it actually demands is given by each bearer out of his own law.

What the next sections establish is what related judgments and actions cannot acquire in the way of structural standing. That is not to say this content makes no other demands. A man can work hard to understand his friend more fully, and that does not offend against what he avowed. What offends is announcing that his own picture is finished, and using it to settle for the friend what the friend truly avows. And offending against it does not mean it will not happen.

3. Twenty Years Does Not Finish the Picture

That man knows his friend better than most. Over twenty years he has seen how the friend chose in several matters, heard what he said, watched the year he changed his mind. He has, in consequence, a fairly fine picture.

The picture may be accurate. It may even be right in every particular. It cannot acquire the verdict finished. And that is not insufficiently fine observation, and not a shortage of material.

What is on the picture falls in two classes, each stopped by something different. One class is whether some content under the friend's name has in fact become his value-content. What would have to be read is first-person avowal, the only place that makes content into value-content — and the outside cannot get into that place. Two candidate signatures were already ruled out: verbal declaration is not necessary, because many value-contents are embodied and tacit; a durable preference is not sufficient, because a liking can hold thirty years and never be claimed.

The other class is readings on the running side: which of his rows can still throw up new candidates in this domain, whether some content is in the candidate field right now, what the organization of this action actually draws on. Reachability is read per row, contents per content, the centre of gravity per action — three subjects, kept apart. And all of those readings are underdetermined before the third person: one and the same visible performance corresponds structurally to several readings that behaviour alone cannot separate.

Both classes were established upstream. The first gives: external evidence does not close into a final criterion. The second gives: underdetermination. Neither reaches a final verdict. A complete picture of him would have to close both. One of them does not close, and the whole picture fails to acquire the verdict complete. Twenty years of attention buys a more accurate picture. It does not buy finished.

What is denied is that verdict, not accuracy. That man may have got it exactly right. He has no way, on third-person evidence, to prove that he got it right, and no way, on that evidence, to prove whether there is something he has not read.

One thing does not go on this list. Whether a row of source is present speaks of a gained source-position, which by definition does not move; the rise and fall of concrete contents speaks of whether they enter the candidate field. Present means different things in the two places, and underdetermination concerns the second. The complete picture spoken of here is limited to concrete contents and readings of running. Which source-positions a bearer has in fact gained belongs to another, structural picture; whether that picture is legible to the third person, this essay does not judge, and the conclusion above does not rest on it.

4. What Can Be Jointly Checked

Beside the things that reach no final verdict, a set of relational conditions can enter joint checking. If there are candidates generated by his own sources, has the relational channel by which they reach expression and discussion been blocked in advance. Can a denial of his be registered as a denial, or is it taken as one more piece of evidence for agreement. Are the roads of refusal, restatement, revision and withdrawal open. All three are facts about the relational structure.

And reading them is not the same as being able to determine. A road being open does not mean he walked it; a road being sealed does not mean there was nothing on his side wanting to come out.

One thing looks similar in form and is not the same. A person's own adjudication takes his existing avowals as its premise and therefore cannot turn round and certify them. That is the first person on himself. The constituting place belongs throughout on his first-person side and never migrates outward; whether it is operable for him at a given moment settles separately, and what can be sealed is the road to it, not the place itself. What he lacks is a tool — taking adjudication to certify avowal is using the wrong thing. Here, in the third person on another, what is lacking is not a tool. It is a place.

Reading through and inferring are also two things. Even if that picture really were finished, one still may not turn it round and say: because I see he has values of his own, he is an end. The rule about the order of inference governs the order; it says nothing about the capacity to read.

None of this depends on anyone having avowed the content of the first two sections. For someone who has avowed it, there is a further layer. However fine the representation, it cannot stand in for the friend's first-person avowal; knowing and constituting were always two things. Treating a fine picture as finished is what this section blocks head-on, and that holds for any third person whatever. What offends against what he avowed is the further step: announcing that the picture is finished, and using it to settle for the friend what he truly avows, so that his later denials and restatements lose all room to rebut. The problem is standing, not accuracy.

5. Which One Matters More

That man has a thing of his own he has worked at for years. Sometimes he wonders: the friend fixing that window, and this thing in my hands — which matters more.

The question has no answer, and the reason is not that the two are too close in weight. To rank the value-standings of two avowed contents under two people, you would need a ruler that does two things at once: stand outside both laws, and convert two first-person standings into one quantity. Neither can be done. Once a thing is the bearer's own and issues from its own law, there is no coordinate system outside that law that could pass a cross-subject verdict of value upon it — and that covers the cross-bearer case. And a content's value-standing takes only holding or not, no quantity. The two layers close here.

There is a polite-sounding move: don't say whose matters more — say both matter equally. It does not hold. Equally is still two gradations on one ruler. It has not removed the ruler; it has only put two readings at the same spot.

What can be said between the two positions is something else. The place that thing occupies in him, and the place this thing occupies in me, are positions of the same type in their respective structures, and they do not constitute a common quantity. Same type says one thing only: each content has taken first-person value-standing in its own bearer. It does not say the two come from the same row of source, does not say they do the same work in their respective days, and certainly does not say they weigh the same.

6. The Ladder in the Yard

What is incomparable is value-standing. Between two people there is no shortage of things that can be looked at together, said together, checked together — including the conditions that matter most for the actual arrangement.

One afternoon two jobs land in one place: whose work has the yard, there is only one ladder, how many days of good weather are left. These are facts in the world, checkable by both sides, and the relevant records can be laid side by side. Where two orders of action meet, what can be arranged is each side's actions — how resources are staggered, who moves the thing that is in the way; and the outside can supply supporting conditions: time, materials, a steadier situation. Doing all that takes rulers, and what they measure is loss, days, one ladder. Those rulers reach the yard. They do not reach standing.

There is a step here that anyone will take without noticing. This plan loses less than that one, therefore the value that argues for this plan matters more than the other. It has to be refuted, because it looks most like common sense.

Its error is not that it is too wide. It is that it switched axes. Consequences say what came out of this one arrangement; value-standing asks whether that content holds in its own bearer's law. Output and position are two independent axes, and the shape is the same one as before: taking something visible in place of something invisible in principle. Substituting the easy for the hard usually works elsewhere; it does not work here, because the reading substituted in does not prove the thing to be proved.

And the standing side does not accept quantity at all. A reading that can be compared for size cannot flow back into a position that takes no quantity.

So two things run at once between two people. On the conditions and consequences in the world, they can look together, check together, and each adjust his arrangement — whether heterogeneous consequences can be converted into one quantity is a further question this essay does not judge. On value-standing they need no ruler and have none, and that is not because they are deferring to each other.

7. “This River Is Ours”

A good many people live by that river. One goes often because he learned to swim there as a child; one makes his living off it; one keeps an old temple on its bank. Over the years they have done several things together: dredged it, stopped a sand-mining operation, pooled money to repair a stretch of embankment. Afterwards they often say: this river is ours in common.

The sentence is right, and it is also blurred. Right, because those things really were done together, following one common arrangement. Blurred, because of where in common lands. Landing on those few undertakings, it says the arrangement of action landed in one place. Landing on the sources, it says these people's value-sources have merged into one.

The second landing does not follow, for three reasons. Each person's source of value is anchored in his standing as an end not being externally placed; for a person running his own law, the running of his sources is anchored in his own law's autonomous reflexive operation. Where it is anchored is a structural fact on his side. Before the day of the dredging, the source of the man who lives off the river was there; after that day it is still there, still in him. Several things done together change nothing on this point.

On the 15DD row, several people's sources can point at each other and cross very densely. Each bearer's 15DD source is still anchored in itself; many sources' pointings crossing does not mean the sources merged into one. Pointing says where toward. It does not say where from.

Dredging together really happened, and the common arrangement is real too. But a relational event is not, by itself, the kind of thing by which any party gains a source-position. Source-positions are given with a bearer's structure. Those joint undertakings do not by themselves change the anchoring of existing sources, and are not enough to show that a new source-position has been gained. Whether a relation can become a condition in some subject's growth is a further question this essay does not judge.

One thing a common relation definitely cannot do has to be said on its own. What those people decided together cannot stand in for any one of them's own avowal. First-person avowal cannot be granted or revoked from outside, and that rule governs exactly this. It governs the content side; where the source is, is another question.

When people say the river is ours, they often also mean something else: protecting this river is a thing each of them has claimed for himself. That layer holds entirely, and is common. Several people each avowing the same thing on his own row is several contents, not one. Same in content, each with its own provenance.

A common content does not become an external ruler by being common. It becomes one at the moment it is taken up to rank people's value-standings, or to declare that someone's value-standing ought to be overridden or revoked. Things done together, rules made together, things kept together are not wrong by virtue of being common.

And if the sources really were merged into one, the first sentence of the spine is gone. His source of value is not mine to give says that source is in him. After merging, the source is in us, and no one can say whose it still is. And what that man avowed takes the first sentence as its object. So merging is not making the relation thicker. It is dismantling that item on his own side. This speaks of a total source taking existing individual sources under it and replacing them; a case that holds separately and coexists with individual sources is not touched by this reductio.

There is a rule of similar shape in the previous essay: a joint decision does not generate a third place of value adjudication. That one says two people settling something does not merge two sets of values into one table and does not produce a place from which either side's order can be set. It falls on the action side and asks whether an adjudicating place has appeared. This section falls on the constituting side and asks where the source is. Similar in shape does not mean one can replace the other.

8. The Window Got Fixed

The window did get fixed. The friend called him over to look, pointed at a few places and said a few words, not many. He stood there and saw more than a repaired window. He saw that this thing is the friend's, that it came out of the friend's own side, and that it was not his to give.

In this example both sides recognized the other. He recognized that the window-fixing is the friend's, out of the friend's side; and the friend recognized that the thing he himself has kept for years is his, out of his side. That layer is given by the example directly — it cannot be read off from who called whom or how much was said, as the earlier section showed. Resonance is mutual recognition, and mutual recognition has two ends.

Resonance happening, and someone judging that it happened, are not the same thing. It can happen and never be named; someone can take a wave of his own feeling for resonance. Descriptions of it can be wrong and can be corrected, and none of that turns round and constitutes it.

The two ends of the recognizing are people, not values. Values do not recognize anything; only bearers can recognize something.

What resonates is each side's values. On the friend's side, what resonates is the window-fixing; which row of source it comes out of is not asked here, and need not be. A concrete content is the occasion on which the recognizing happens, not the object of what is recognized. It is the values each gives that can resonate, with no restriction to a row. Two people can recognize each other over a craft, over a stretch of caring, over a long wait, over a preference whose provenance neither can name.

What is recognized is always the same thing: that is his, out of his side, not mine to give. Not that the contents are the same. Sameness of structure gives the possibility of recognizing; it does not guarantee sameness of content. Two people can care about very different things and still recognize each other in the ownness on each side.

The possibility comes from sameness of structure. Every subject's law is laid down by itself. Neither can take, from an external position, a final exhaustive verdict on the other's law, and neither can write the other's law by proxy — and yet the two laws are formally the same in structure: the same inner double negation recurs in every self-legislating subject. Value and law share that structure. Sameness of structure gives a structure that can be recognized; the recognizing is still performed by a bearer. It is precisely because the same structure recurs between subject and subject that the values each gives can resonate at all. No ruler is at work here. A ruler ranks; resonance recognizes.

9. “Can Have” and “Has”

The spine says he can have values of his own. This section says he has. The one word's difference is real. Can have does not wait on his actually giving anything — a baby who cannot yet say what he wants is inside that sentence too. Resonance requires that he really gave something, for me to recognize. Acknowledgment can be directed at an other not yet present; resonance cannot. It needs something given and seen.

So can have reaches further than has. There are people between whom and me no expression, work or relational trace will ever pass; resonance will not happen there, and every one of them is inside the spine's sentence. Resonance is what the spine looks like when it is cashed out at a meeting. It is not the whole of the spine.

Whether it resonates also depends on expression, on the relation, and on first-person uptake. Sameness of structure gives only the possibility. If the friend that day had not given that thing in any form that could be received, or had given it and the other had not recognized it, or if something else already stood between them, that moment would not have come.

Nor is it anyone's demand for action. One party's request or command cannot constitute resonance, and cannot make it happen one-sidedly. What one party can do is give or keep the conditions: give time, give materials, give a steadier situation, move the thing that is in the way. All of that can be done, and doing it does not guarantee the moment comes.

A value no one resonates with is not thereby demoted. What resonates is already complete in a solitary subject. That window was the friend's, all through the years when no one came to look at it.

The moment is a real event; it is between two people and has a place of its own. And it does not enter the source-figure. It makes no third value, no third source, and no third bearer. The recognizing happens between two people already present and their values already present. The pearl was there before the resonance.

10. Joint Audit

Resonance cannot be brought off by one party alone. There is something else two people can do together, and do with real purchase: joint audit.

The earlier section put the two sides apart: the other's internal state of avowal and his readings of running reach no final verdict; the opening and closing of certain relational channels can enter joint checking. Joint audit works only on the second side.

It has three parts. Each party can speak only for his own side, from the first-person place, and answers only for his own side. That statement cannot be written by anyone else, and entering a joint setting does not give it a guarantee. A person does not necessarily know on the spot where one of his contents came from; and a person's own adjudication cannot turn round and certify his existing avowals. Joint audit gives no guarantee at that layer.

What the two check together is the opening and closing of relational channels. If there are candidates, is the channel by which they reach expression and discussion open; can a denial be registered as a denial; are the roads of refusal, restatement, revision and withdrawal open. Those three can be checked by both sides, and the records can be laid side by side. His internal state of avowal is not checked, and actual reachability is not checked either.

What comes out is two first-person statements each party answers for, plus one jointly checked record of relational conditions. Where the two sides do not match, register only that they do not match. Do not first judge which side is wrong, and do not first judge that some road is sealed. A mismatch can come from the two seeing different things, from one not having put it accurately this time, from the two standing in structurally asymmetric places in this relation — and it can come from the road really being sealed. To judge that a road is sealed in running, further relational evidence is required. With the evidence in, the conclusion still takes the form of places and channels: this road is still open, that road is sealed in running, or the three are not yet complete. Cannot-determine is itself a legitimate conclusion.

When one says a road is sealed, what is sealed is the road to that place, not the place itself. Claiming, revision and withdrawal are structurally permanent, and colonization acts on reachability, not on presence.

This upper bound is not added here. An audit that reaches past those three to read the first person generates, structurally, exactly the relation introjection requires. Joint audit runs below that line.

Each party can also state, from the first-person place, and answer for, whether the recognizing on his own side is complete. For the other side, what he gets is a relational reading, fallible and revisable. Two people can also say together that resonance happened here — a sentence that may hold and may be a misjudgment. Neither party nor any joint procedure can raise it into a final verdict. This essay gives no procedure for determining whether resonance occurred, and that is not to say no one can answer the question.

11. The Other Who Has Not Yet Appeared

One case needs no one present. A person can work toward an other who has not appeared — write a book, leave a craft behind, cut a road through. A solitary subject keeps that formal other-place reserved for any bearer of ends that may come; what it avows is a content of the same form as the spine: any bearer, should he appear, can have values of his own, and this is not mine to give. That item is real, and the person writing the book is writing by it.

And the sentence about one particular actual other has not yet held. That is an anticipatory enactment toward the formal other-place; it does not fill the fact-place. Only an actually existing particular other within the domain of bearers can fill the fact-place of an actual other is also an end. The first subject in a universe, if it has already avowed that conditional from the 15DD place, has a real content of its own, and the actual-other place is still empty; when a second subject appears, that only lands the fact-place on a particular person. Whether the first subject avows that fact as its own item still requires a further first-person response.

This has to be kept apart from the baby. A bearer who does not yet exist can only enter as a conditional: if he appears, he can have values of his own, and this is not mine to give. The baby is not that case. He already fills the fact-place of an actual other. How far the concrete value-contents under his name have got is not judged by whether he can speak — speech was never a necessary signature of avowal. That he cannot yet be the first-person avowing party of this item does not mean that of him only can have may be said.

12. What Remains

The other's value is not my value; that the other can have values of his own, and that this is not mine to give, is my value. The second takes the first as its object. What the first states held before my avowing it; whether I avow it is a first-person occurrence on my side, and not avowing does not make the thing untrue.

The three limits are one thing read at three ranges, and each stands on its own grounds; none follows from another.

Written short — cannot be read through, cannot be compared, cannot be merged — the three still do not entail everyone lives their own life. A limit says which operations I do not have on another's values. It does not say there is no relation between him and me. Recognition happens exactly inside these three, and is not generated by them. Its two ends are given by two bearers and their respective values; the three block one party from settling the other's account with his own representation, block an external ruler from passing verdict on both sides' standing, and block the kind of merging that takes existing individual sources under it and replaces them, erasing the source-end. The three say what resonance cannot be written as. They do not guarantee that resonance will come.

Two relational forms remain, and they do not do the same work. Resonance can happen: a request or a command cannot constitute it and cannot make it happen one-sidedly; what one party can do is give or keep the conditions. Joint audit can be done: it runs on the relational-channel side, does not reach either party's internal state of avowal, and gives neither party a guarantee he issues to himself.

How the other can have values of his own and this is not mine to give goes on being borne by one and the same life belongs to the theory of meaning.

Abstract

Three essays in, the synchronic figure is up, the entrance to occurrence is up, and the reading of those places when they are violated is up. What is missing is time. Every time an earlier essay met the question how does this change as it runs, it handed the question forward to this one.

Three things enter time: the reachability of a source, concrete contents, and the centre of gravity. A source-position once gained is not among them — within the range where the bearer's structure stands, its presence no longer varies.

What most needs guarding against here is not saying too little. It is building a machine. The grammar of dynamics wants a source of motive power, and this system has none: a source is a structural ground, not a supply end for contents, and avowal and uptake are completed in the first person, where no external description reaches. So every explanation takes one form: which places were open at the time, which road was reachable at the time. Conditions can be listed, and conditions are necessary without being sufficient. Where they fall short is not a debt the explanation owes. It is exactly where the bearer stands.

And one cut has to be held throughout: accumulation and diachrony are not the same thing. The same running repeated many times is accumulation. One constituting act not yet complete in time is diachrony. Constitution is not reached by accumulation, and constitution can be diachronic. Running is the other way round — it comes in a spectrum, and accumulation in time can make it deeper or shallower.

1. Three Things Enter Time

Within the range where the bearer's structure stands, a value-source once gained has its presence unvarying from the moment of gaining: not with the arising and passing of concrete contents, not with the rise and fall of reachability, not with the shifting of the centre of gravity. This does not say a person has one and the same set of source-positions for life. What dimension-opening does is add a source-position on top of the old ones; it adds, and does not alter what is already there. What has been gained is not thereafter reduced.

Precisely because those do not move, the other three can be read as rises and falls rather than as the thing itself coming into and going out of existence. A content faded and that row of source is still there, so it is a fading and not a vanishing. Reachability has somewhere to come back to, so it is called gaining. Going back costs nothing, because what a cost would have to be measured against never moved at all. Three sentences, one fact underneath.

What is unvarying is the presence of a source-position already gained, not its running. A bearer voiding a higher source whose conditions of application have actually arrived voids that row's reachability; the row is still there, and so is the history of construction. What can be sealed is the road to them, not the things themselves.

The three readings have different subjects. Reachability is read per row of source: in this domain, can any candidate out of that row still surface. Content is read per content: is this one in the candidate field right now, is it at the centre of gravity. The centre of gravity is read per action: what did the organization of this action actually draw on. The three subjects are not on one level. So the three together are not a state vector — you cannot combine their values freely like coordinates, and there is no transition rule taking one set of values to the next.

Only one direction of inference holds among them: if an action has a centre-of-gravity reading, then at least one avowed content on that row is taking part in organizing the action. No other direction holds — and least of all reachability from the centre of gravity. A man can go on living by the one thing he avowed long ago while that row throws up nothing new at all. Reachability asks whether new candidates out of that row can still surface; an avowed content taking part in organizing an action is an existing draw, and is no evidence of that row's current reachability.

2. No Motor

Why a content occurs at this moment and not that one: the answer here does not take the form what pushed it. It takes the form which places were open at the time, which road was reachable.

This is not to say conditions do not matter. Experience, the body, relations, a work encountered — any of these can be the condition of an avowal or an uptake. What is refused is two other things: an engine built into the source, and a transition law that computes constitution completed out of conditions.

The reason was already given when the source was raised: a source is a structural ground, not a causal origin producing contents, and not a store or supply end for them. A supply end can be asked how much it outputs, when, and how fast. A structural ground admits none of those questions. Writing the dynamics as a law of output amounts to changing the source, on the ontological figure, into something else.

Conditions can be listed, and conditions are necessary without being sufficient: list them all and the event can still fail to happen. That is not a debt the explanation owes. And the gap is not there waiting for a stronger cause to fill it. It is where this structure is simply open. The bearer stands there.

Nor can it be closed by adding more conditions. Set up a condition for applying the conditions, and that one has itself to be applied to the case; the gap has only moved to the next line of the list. A list does not close by getting longer.

The first critique established the same shape at the working end: applying a rule to a case cannot itself be given by a rule. There it is the operator's cut; here it is a bearer's uptake of a bridge of his own. Same shape, not reducible to each other.

3. Accumulation and Diachrony

However long, accumulation gives no content a position it did not gain in constitution. Habituation produces no ownership, long holding produces no avowal, and long interruption revokes none. The colonization essay established a special case of the same sentence: repeated claiming produces no source; run it ten thousand times and it still produces none. The reason there was not that repetition is weak. It is that what it names lies on the side of constitution.

But constitution can be diachronic. Some avowals occur in a moment; some take shape by degrees and settle only after years. A person often has to try living a thing for a while before it settles, and what happens during that while is not the gathering of evidence — it is avowal itself taking shape by degrees. There is no conflict with the paragraph above, because accumulation and diachrony are two things: accumulation is one kind of running repeated many times; diachrony is one constituting act not yet finished.

From outside the two look alike. A man does the same thing for ten years. Those ten years can be one kind of running repeated many times, with that thing never claimed by him in his own law. They can equally be one avowal taking shape across those ten years and settling somewhere in them. What is seen from outside is the same ten years.

Running, on the other side, does accumulate, and usually that is exactly how it changes. Reachability can be impaired by degrees and can be restored by degrees. What is said is the direction of change, not where the line falls.

Constituting and recognizing a constituting are two things. Constituting completes when it happens. Recognizing it may be simultaneous, or may come later in the running and in retrospect; there is no general order. And recognizing does not constitute: once a constituting act is complete it is complete, and a later recognition neither makes it happen nor makes it count. Coming early or late alters nothing about what has already been done — and never finding an occasion to draw on it does not make it not have happened.

4. Underdetermined from Outside

Every reading this essay gives is underdetermined before the third person: one and the same visible performance corresponds, structurally, to several different readings, and those readings cannot be told apart by behaviour alone.

This is not insufficiently fine observation, and not a shortage of material. It has two roots.

The first: claiming, revision and withdrawal are first-person constituting acts, and there is no set of external signatures both necessary and sufficient and portable to someone else. Two candidates were already ruled out. Verbal declaration is not necessary, because many value-contents are embodied and tacit. A durable preference is not sufficient, because a liking can hold thirty years and never be claimed. More generally, the third person cannot exhaustively verify whether an avowal occurred, so external evidence does not close into a final criterion. Facts about the relational structure really are readable: whether the candidate field is filled, whether a denial can be registered as a denial, whether the paths of revision and withdrawal are open. Reading those is not the same as being able to determine.

The second: even on the observable side, the variables of running fall on a spectrum, and there is no identifiable point on that spectrum where the line lies. Whether it has been crossed cannot, at the margin, be read off by a finer rule. It has to be judged case by case.

The colonization essay set an upper bound from the criterion side: an audit that oversteps generates, structurally, the very relation introjection requires. What is set here has the same root on the other side — there the limit is how far audit can go; here it is what form explanation may take.

Hence a general rule: this essay gives no decision procedure that infers constitution sufficiently from third-person evidence, and no final test. This is not modesty. It is a direct corollary of the two roots. Facts about the relational structure can be distinguished, and distinguishing them does not convert into determining constitution; between the two steps stands the previous essay's sentence. Anything made out of these readings into a ruler to hold up against another person is not the thing established here.

5. What Reachability Is

A road is reachable when, in some content-domain, candidates out of one of the bearer's own rows of value-source can still surface from his own working and enter the candidate field.

A source gives a shape, not a candidate. A structural position gives, by its structure, the form in which a class of value can land there — as the shape of a socket decides what can fit into it. So saying a candidate comes out of a row of source says it fitted that shape, not that the row produced it. The surfacing itself is, throughout, the bearer's own working.

Reachability is read per row of source, not per content. It asks whether new candidates out of that row can still surface in this domain. It does not ask whether any have surfaced right now, and it does not ask whether the ones already claimed are still in use. A road reachable with nothing surfacing at the moment is ordinary — a man goes a stretch with no particular thoughts about something, and that does not mean the road is cut. Conversely, a road unreachable does not mean the domain stands empty; usually it is not empty at all, only that everything that gets in comes from elsewhere. Can surface and has surfaced are two things.

Reachability is also not presence. The presence of a gained source-position is the thing that does not move; reachability is the thing that does. Colonization acts always on reachability and never on presence. A man's road on some row can be obstructed for a long time, and this domain go long without one candidate out of it, and the row is still there.

Reachability falls on the side of running, so it comes in a spectrum: the road can be clear, and it can be obstructed. And on that spectrum there is no identifiable point where the line between reachable and unreachable lies. What is sayable is the direction of change — that a row's reachability is being impaired by degrees, or recovering by degrees. What is not sayable is how far it has got, and no case's line may be carried over and applied to another. At the margin, judge case by case.

One relation to the previous essay should be marked. Occupation is defined as a domain sealed by an external end until no candidate out of one's own rows can be got. Reachability is the same question on the affirmative side. But unreachability does not arise only from occupation: occupation is the variety of unreachability sealed shut by an external end, not the whole of it.

6. Four Men

That no candidate out of one's own rows can surface in a domain — this state, by itself, judges nothing. What has to be asked is what maintains it. And there can be more than one maintainer: one and the same seal can be propped from outside and kept by the bearer himself at once. So the question has an order. First: is anything outside maintaining it? If yes, it goes to the externally maintained kind, and does not move out of it because the bearer is also keeping it. If no, is he maintaining it himself? If still no, it is the kind where the conditions no longer obtain. The three are not an added taxonomy. They are the three answers this one question falls to in order.

The three look identical from outside, so they have to be set side by side. Take the 15DD domain. Four men, and from outside none of them any longer does, for the people near him, the things one only does by taking the other as an end.

The first man genuinely has no one near him. He moved a few times, the old ties broke, and the new place has not grown any relations yet. The actual other this row requires is not present, and no candidate out of his own row can surface in this domain.

The second man has someone near him — that person is right in front of him — and he keeps everything he has carried along the way, and he has voided this person's standing as an end entirely.

The third man has someone near him. And in the matter of how to treat people, every practice he can bring himself to name comes from a set of rules picked up elsewhere; what surfaces from his own working cannot get into this domain's candidate field.

The fourth man, from very early on, has had in the matter of how to treat people only one set of practices given by others. A candidate out of his own row has never once surfaced in this domain.

Four men in the same state, with different maintainers.

In the first, no one is maintaining it. The conditions that carry this row's running no longer obtain: the field is gone, the people one did the thing with are not there, the bodily or temporal conditions changed. What is said here is that a whole row throws up no candidate of one's own, not that some particular content no longer surfaces — that latter is the rise and fall of contents. No external end is maintaining anything here, and the colonization criterion correctly fails to reach it. It is not pathology and not a defect. It is a person's circumstances changing in time.

In the second, the bearer maintains it himself. He actively voids a higher source whose conditions of application have actually arrived — the active closing marked off from neutral going-back. The conditions having actually arrived is, in his case, that the particular other is already in front of him; that is exactly what separates this from a plain going-back, where the condition is not present. There are people near him and no external end maintaining this voiding, so it does not fall under the colonization judgment. What it changes is that row's reachability, not its presence: the history of construction cannot be erased. What is voided is the running, not the fact that the row was once gained.

In the third, it is maintained from outside. The third man and the fourth are both here: something occupies this domain's candidate field, and that something is propped from outside. This cell goes to the colonization essay to be judged, and the reading there is asymmetric — three signatures complete, the reading of external colonization in this domain is determinate; an irrefutable attribution absent, that branch does not hold, determinately; attribution present with occupation or locking incomplete, the third person stops at cannot-determine, which is neither a weaker positive nor a negative.

The three readings differ, and none of them moves the case out of this kind: what is propped from outside does not disappear because a branch was excluded, nor because the reading was cannot-determine. So this essay does not loosen that narrow criterion, and does not coin a name for the ones that could not be determined.

Higher, here, means structural order of position — presupposing more, later in the order of unfolding. It is not a ranking of value. A content falling in a source-domain later in the structural order is not thereby weightier, and a bearer drawing on it is not thereby higher in value-standing.

Put together, the three give one result: unreachability is not uniformly pathology. The same state is, in one kind, circumstances having changed; in another, the man himself having closed it; and only in the third is it the colonization essay's business to judge.

7. Gaining Is Not Retrieving

This section is about the gaining of reachability, not its recovery. Recovery is one cell of it — the cell where there was something before.

In the fourth man there is no before to go back to. On the shape of his own row, no candidate has ever surfaced from his own working. If one day the first such candidate takes a position in this domain, that too is a gaining of reachability — and it is nothing coming back. Calling the whole thing recovery implies there was an original waiting to be retrieved, and that is exactly what the colonization essay blocked when it pinned discovery down: discovery means only a content taking a position under one of one's own rows, not finding an existing item.

And in the cell where there was something before, what is gained is not standing. The belonging of a place is permanent, and what colonization can do is make claiming, revision and withdrawal unreachable in running. So no one needs to give the bearer back the standing to claim, because no one took it. What is restored is running. Same grammar as going-back: what goes back is the running, not the history of construction. What is constitutive is not abolished by a relational act, and therefore is not returned by one either.

8. What the Outside Can Stop

Whether the outside has any purchase here is settled not by which place is sealed but by the same question as before: who maintains the seal. The three cells give three answers.

Where no one maintains it, there is nothing to release. The first man's domain throws up no candidate because the conditions are gone; that was never pathology, and there is nothing to undo.

Where he maintains it himself, there is nothing that can be stopped. The voiding is the second man's own doing; no one outside is holding it down. Others can still be right in front of him, that other can still be present, and the row still throws up nothing. The outside is not without work to do — it can be present, it can ask, it can make that condition of application arise, again and again. What it does not have is an act that could revoke this voiding.

Where the outside maintains it, something is being propped, and there is therefore a form in which it can stop. What is being maintained differs by case, and there are three seals.

One seals the provenance of candidates. That single set of rules fills this domain's candidate field, so that what does not come from it cannot get in. It is maintained from outside; ceasing to fill it is the release.

One seals the channel of rebuttal for one attribution. The community says of some content that this person has claimed it as his value, and his denial of that attribution cannot be registered as a denial within the relational structure. Whether an attribution is present, and whether a denial can be registered as a denial, are facts about the relational structure that the third person can read; making it registrable again is likewise a matter of the relational structure.

One seals the whole of the paths of reflection, restatement, revision and withdrawal. This differs from the last: that one sealed only the rebuttal of one attribution; this one seals whether he can change anything at all.

All three are propped from outside, and all three have a form in which they stop. Stop all three and the state no longer holds: once the attribution occupying the constitutive place is withdrawn and can be denied, that content falls back to being a candidate and is no longer taken as constitution completed. The reading on the bearer's side was indeed occupied too — and that is a structural matter, not his subjective assent; being structural, it fails along with what was propping it.

The outside's purchase ends there, and where it ends is not here. After that content falls back to being a candidate, whether it then becomes his value is a further step: it has to take a position under one of his own rows. Dissolving does nothing for that step; it only clears the seat. And no external act can perform that step by proxy. The outside can still hand over candidates, demonstrate, clarify, get the conditions of occurrence ready — and taking a position under one of his own rows is a step only he can walk.

And one branch does not dissolve along with it. If the case also involves an external warrant counterfeiting the standing of one's own source-domain, that branch is not automatically dissolved by the release of relational conditions: what props it is not anyone in the relation but a standing that stops outside — and that branch's only tense is retrospect. A change in relational conditions can be the occasion for a retrospect. It cannot substitute for one. The two branches can coexist in one case, and neither follows from the other, nor dissolves with it.

So the line can be written in a sentence. Releasing conditions is an act whose result is not decided by the one who performs it; whereas the three seals stand up without needing any cooperation from the receiving side. Fill the candidate field, fix a content as constituted, void the revisable place — those three, once standing, make the seal stand. They can come from one person's arrangement, or be propped jointly by a stretch of relations no one is coordinating; what is judged is the state, not whose handiwork it is. And what they set up is a seal, not a constituting: whether a content was ever claimed in the bearer's own law, that seal does not decide by a hair. While stopping the filling, withdrawing the attribution, giving back the paths of revision — when all of that is done, nothing has been completed. Whether any candidate out of his own rows can surface in that domain, and whether he claims what surfaces, is entirely his.

It follows that handing in a candidate is not making reachability be gained. It is not overstepping — a demonstration, a clarification, a work encountered are all everyday shaping; they put candidates into the receiver's field, and whether the content becomes his value-content still rests on his avowal. Handing in a candidate is not the gaining of reachability, not because it ought not be done, but because it is not what it does. Reachability asks whether candidates out of his own row can surface in this domain, and the one handed in did not surface from his working.

One asymmetry has to be written down. The outside can give back the operability of the revisable place; the revising can still only be done by the bearer in the first person. The first is clearing the road, the second is walking it. Neither substitutes for the other: road cleared and no one walks, no revision happened; and if he would walk while the road is locked, the step has nowhere to land.

A last limit. Conditions complete does not guarantee that the gaining occurs. The permanence of a place gives a place belonging to the bearer; it gives no attainment and no timetable. And who is entitled to do the releasing, to what degree, and whether releasing ought to be encouraged, are normative questions this essay does not draw on.

9. Two Cuts on Fading

An avowed content has faded. The sentence holds from outside, and underneath it there can be three different things. Two cuts tell them apart.

The first cut asks: was there a first-person constituting act in this change? If not, it is a rise or fall in running — the content may not be entering the current candidate field, or it may be entering and not at the centre of gravity. Either way, its standing as this bearer's value-content has not changed. If yes, go to the second cut.

The second cut asks: has the original claiming terminated? Not terminated: revision. Terminated: withdrawal.

Two cuts, not three items in a row. The three outcomes are not on one side to begin with: a rise or fall in running is on the running side, while revision and withdrawal are both on the constituting side — which is the essay's opening cut. Lay the three out as three level options and you read them as peers, and hide that cut.

A man has hardly played the piano these past few years. The sentence holds from outside, and underneath it there are three things — and between the first and the other two stands the first cut: in the first nothing constitutive happened at all; in the other two something did.

One: he still holds playing as his own, and simply has not played much these years. The place is open, he has nothing he wants to change, he just has not played.

Two: he still claims it, and it is no longer the same one. What it used to be was becoming someone who could take the stage; what it is now is playing weekly with a few people. The old shape no longer appears, so from outside it reads as fading — and the claiming has not terminated. What changed is the content itself. This is revision.

Three: he no longer claims it. If he sits down at the piano again after this, that is another matter. This is withdrawal.

The three look identical from outside. The judgment does not rest on the state but on what happened in this change, and whether the original claiming is still there.

10. Not Lost by Disuse, Not Gained by Resemblance

An avowed content does not lose its standing by long absence from running. Standing changes only by revision or withdrawal — not by the passage of time, and not by attention moving away.

This is the mirror, at the level of content, of the source–occurrence decoupling: there, a source's presence is not lost with the rise and fall of contents; here, a content's standing is not lost with the rise and fall of its own running.

On the not-terminated branch, what comes back is its re-entering the candidate field, or its re-taking the centre of gravity; nothing happens at the constitutive place. A content revised along the way stays on this branch, because the claiming did not terminate. The withdrawn branch is different: what appears now is a candidate. How much it resembles the earlier one gives it nothing. Resemblance does not inherit constitution; it has to pass first-person avowal again to become this person's value-content.

All three men take up the piano again ten years later. In the first two, what comes back is the same avowed content — in the second, in its revised shape. In the third, what appears is a candidate; however much it resembles what he once claimed, it still has to go through his own law again. From outside they look identical: all three are playing again after ten years.

Maintenance and investment, handed forward from the previous essay, settle here. They are facts on the running side, not conditions on the constituting side. Sustained investment changes how often a content enters the candidate field and whether it holds the centre of gravity; it neither changes nor consolidates its standing, and long non-investment does not diminish it. So the two words can be used freely: they were never about constitution, and need not borrow the name of valuing.

No external criterion of identity is set here — that is, whether what surfaces now counts as the same content is not decided by degree of resemblance. Whether it counts is decided by how far that claiming itself reaches, and that is a first-person matter: what falls within its reach was already his content and needs no re-taking; what falls outside it is a candidate however alike, and must pass avowal again. On the withdrawn branch the question does not arise: the claiming has terminated, and reaches nothing.

The distinction between the branches must be kept, though. It blocks the thought that a withdrawn content automatically resumes its place by surfacing again. Withdrawal is real. As for which branch a given case falls on, look at what the claiming reaches — and only he can answer that. The answer may come at once, or may have to wait until he looks back.

11. Neither Change nor Stability Is a Criterion

The colonization essay established one negative: revision and change are not evidence of colonization, and reading he changed as a sign of he was colonized is reading the norm as pathology.

The positive half has to be narrowed. A content faded, another rose, the centre shifted — these are rises and falls in running, and they do not prove the revisable place is open: with the place locked, contents rise and fall all the same. What does have proving force is something else: that a first-person revision or withdrawal was actually carried out. That proves the place is operable now, and cannot prove in reverse that it was never locked before.

Stability proves nothing either. A content untouched for ten years may be a place open with nothing he wanted to change, or a place locked and nothing he could change. The two look identical from outside.

So neither change nor stability serves as a criterion of colonization. Nor does the amount of change, since that would require identifying a point on a spectrum, and there is no such point.

12. The Centre of Gravity

The centre of gravity is which row of source the organization of one action actually draws on.

It is read per action, and it has a domain of definition: only an action organized by contents the bearer has avowed has a centre of gravity to read. An action organized solely by external requirement, by habitual reaction, or by a script that has taken no standing in his own law gets no centre-of-gravity reading here. The restriction is not optional. Forcing a reading amounts to retroactively certifying something occupied as the running of one of his own rows — which is exactly what the whole middle of this essay is blocking. No reading does not mean low value, and does not mean the action does not count.

Within that domain, any action can be asked which row it draws on, and the question needs no stretch of time and no window. It need not be unique — one action can draw on several rows at once. It need not be stable — two consecutive actions drawing on different rows says nothing in itself; a person without a stable centre of gravity is not thereby defective.

Saying his centre of gravity lately is on such a row already contains a vague window and has already gathered many readings together. What comes out of the gathering is a description, not the centre of gravity as defined here; nor does it thereby become another state the bearer is in.

So this essay does not ask how long counts, or how many times counts, and sets no uniform measure for the centre of gravity. The reason is not that it cannot be counted: how many of the last ten actions drew on a given row is perfectly countable. The reason is that what you counted is not the centre of gravity. The centre of gravity is read per action and done; it does not accumulate into a further state on top of those counts. And taking such counts and ranking people by them runs into another block: being an end does not rank, and quantities of this kind have no place to sit in value-standing.

13. The Centre Converts into No Ranking

Richness and the centre of gravity fall on two levels. Richness falls at the level of presence and the history of construction: the breadth of value-dimensions operable for the bearer himself, accumulating with the history of construction and not erasable. The centre of gravity falls at the level of running, free to move, and going back in running costs nothing in value. The two do not imply each other: using few right now does not change the breadth already gained in the history of construction, and having gained much does not require using much right now.

So which row an action's organization draws on has nothing to do with the bearer's value-standing.

The question a reader most wants to ask at this point is am I regressing. The question's presupposition does not hold. It presupposes that the centre of gravity moving toward rows earlier in the structural order could be a loss, and that cannot be a loss: structural order is not value order, and going back costs nothing. This is not a refusal to answer. It is that what the question asks about has no place in the structure.

The centre moving away also comes in two kinds that look identical from outside. In one, the row is intact and this stretch of actions simply is not organized out of it. In the other, that row is already unreachable and throws nothing up. The first says nothing at all; the second sends you back to ask what maintains the seal. Their external appearance can be exactly the same.

One more thing on this level works the same way. After a particular value-demand is met, that domain may go on producing new demands, or may produce no more. Neither changes the source — a source does not grow because demands keep coming, or shrink because they cease — and neither changes the bearer's value-standing. It is said here only that both happen; not which is better.

14. Output and Position Are Two Axes

What a person made, learned, left behind — these are legitimate objects of dynamics, and discussing them violates nothing. What was refused was using them as a criterion, not discussing them.

The two axes do not imply each other. Where the places are open there can be years with nothing to show; a relation that falls under the colonization criterion can come with considerable achievement. A man inside an appraisal-grammar that is in no way his own can make a great deal, and make it well; a man on the row he avowed can go a long time making nothing.

There is one inference readers actually make: there is output, so it is not colonization. That one has to be refuted, because it looks most like common sense. Its error is not that it is too wide. It is that it switched axes: output says what came out of that place; the criterion asks whose end occupies that place. A relation can both have an external end at the constitutive place and really have got this person to make a good deal. The two hold separately, diminish nothing in each other, and prove nothing about each other.

Block the other directions with it. No output does not show that this was not really his value-content. No output does not show the place is sealed. An open place does not guarantee output. And a colonization holding does not mean there was necessarily no development there.

Taking output as the criterion is really taking something visible in place of something invisible in principle. Output is right there for anyone to read, and a constituting act has no necessary and sufficient external signature. Substituting the easy for the hard usually works elsewhere; it does not work here, because the reading you substituted in does not prove the thing to be proved.

Development here means observable results in capacity, work, or institutions. It does not mean dimension-opening, and it does not mean a rise in value-standing. Neither of those is on this axis at all.

15. The Occasion of Dimension-Opening

Why an opening is taken up at this moment and not another: two conditions can be listed.

One is the structural premise: the remainder of the current construct gives a legitimate bridge. This one does not vary with the moment; while it is there it is there.

One is the occasional condition: the conditions of application of that row of source actually arise. This is what answers why now and not then. At 15DD it is a particular other having entered the relational field.

Both conditions present and no uptake occurring is legitimate. Two people's current constructs leave the same bridge, and each has a particular other standing in the relational field; one takes it up and one does not. Same structural premise, same occasional condition, different events. This is not a missing condition. Adding one would not close it, because that one has itself to be applied to the case; the gap has only moved to the next line.

The word reachability is not borrowed here. Reachability asks whether candidates out of an existing row can surface in a domain, and a bridge points at a source-position not yet gained; a source one does not have admits no question of reachability. It follows that occupation cannot reach a bridge either: that line is drawn at not being able to get a candidate out of one of one's own rows in this domain, and a bridge is not a candidate under any existing row. A bridge can in fact go unmet; a person can go a lifetime without meeting such a situation. And not meeting it is not colonization — just as the man with no one near him is not colonized. The colonization criterion does not cover this; the address is marked and no new line is drawn.

Uptake can occur only from the bearer's first person. The question left open when valuing was raised — why a bearer takes up at just this moment — is answered here on the side of conditions, not on the side of causes.

Whether an opening is complete has no external criterion independent of first-person uptake. Two words have to be kept apart here, and what separates them is not time but object. Awareness has as its object what is happening this moment: a man can know what he is doing now, and know that it is not light for him. Determination has another object: whether what happened this moment was in fact an uptake. The two can be simultaneous, or far apart; there is no general order.

What uptake gains is a source-position. And a source-position is not the whole class of contents that have appeared; it is the shape that lets a whole class take a position. So the position can be recognized without waiting for the whole class actually to appear. If this once has already shown a new shape, the bearer may know it right then; if it has shown only one content whose reach is still unclear, that waits on later contents to make it plain.

Later running is its appearing, not its constituting. A man can, at some moment, resolutely treat another as an end, and the thing is done at that moment; if he never again meets an occasion that draws on that row, the uptake still happened, and is not retroactively deemed not to have happened by later scarcity. So what determination waits on is appearing, not constituting: it waits for a thing already done to show what it is, not for it to be done.

A cannot-but so strong the bearer cannot himself explain it is a first-person thread, not a criterion. It cannot determine a new source-position: every construct carries a remainder, and being unable to explain may be only that remainder, or only that he has not yet stated the old source's boundary clearly. Conversely, a real uptake need not be inexplicable; the bearer may perfectly well say it in the old words to hand. A thread stays a thread. It can let him know almost at once, and it does not thereby become a ruler to judge with.

And whether he knows at once or recognizes it only later, knowing does not constitute: uptake happened when it happened, and a later determination neither makes it happen nor makes it count.

16. Uptake Is Not an Obligation

A bearer with a legitimate bridge in front of him may decline to take it up, at no loss whatever in value-standing. A person can live his whole life within the rows of source he currently has, and that is entirely self-consistent. This was established earlier; it is a direct corollary of not ranking.

It has to be raised again here, because the preceding sections listed so many conditions that they can read like an indication of where one ought to go. They are not. Conditions are for reading how a thing happens, not for saying that it ought to happen. A remainder gives a shape; it gives no compulsion. No remainder forces the next cut.

The first critique established the same direction elsewhere: can be advanced is a capacity, not an obligation. Same direction, not reducible to each other.

17. What Remains

When one bearer's several avowed contents demand incompatible actions, how it is adjudicated belongs to the essay on conflict. This essay gives each one's reading in time; it does not give how they are settled when they meet.

Why another's value cannot be exhaustively read belongs to the essay on the other. The external underdetermination established here is that limit showing itself on the dynamics side.

How an avowed content moves toward action is the entrance to the theory of action. Judgment belongs there in its entirety; this essay does not use it and passes no verdict on it.

This essay gives readings in time; it gives no normative force. Whether the gaining of reachability ought to be encouraged, who is entitled to release those conditions and to what degree, whether a man's active voiding of a higher source whose conditions have arrived ought to be discouraged, whether a domain going on producing demands or ceasing to should be recommended, what place output's reading has in practical evaluation — the address is marked and nothing more.

Of the four things, only one does not move. Within the range where the bearer's structure stands, a value-source once gained has its presence unvarying: not lessened by a content fading, not by the centre moving away, not extinguished by an act of active voiding. Dimension-opening can add a source-position on top of the old ones, and what has been gained is thereafter only added to. What enters time is reachability, concrete contents, the centre of gravity — and the reason their rises and falls can be read as rises and falls is exactly that the unmoving things are there.

There is no motor in time here. Reachability impaired or gained, contents fading or returning, the centre moving about — these do vary with conditions, and no engine built into the source is pushing them, and no transition law computes events out of conditions. They are what the opening and shutting of places, and the holding or failing of conditions, look like in time; and however completely conditions are listed they do not entail a constituting, and where the list falls short is exactly where the bearer stands. What time can do is let a state of running deepen or thin, let an unfinished constituting act have room to finish, let a thing already done show what it did. It cannot claim for anyone, cannot make a content someone's by lasting, and cannot make it no longer someone's by interruption.

And all of these readings are underdetermined from outside. So what this essay gives is a way of reading, not a ruler.
