8. Occupation

Occupation is the candidate field arranged from outside to this degree: in some content-domain, the bearer can no longer get a candidate out of any row of his own sources. There are two ways to reach the threshold. The endogenous road is pressed shut, so that nothing in this domain surfaces out of his own working. Or the outside road is filled by a single effective grammar of appraisal, so that candidates not issuing from that grammar cannot enter. Both point at one thing: in this domain, every available candidate comes from one place, and that place is not the bearer.

The threshold belongs to the place of appearance and does not borrow locking's. Locking asks whether refusal, reconstruction and revision have any room left. Occupation asks whether the candidates have a second source. They can hold independently.

The threshold clause is part of the criterion. Arranging what someone sees first is neither remarkable nor harmful in itself. A good demonstration arranges what you see first too: a skilled hand sets a craft in front of you, a work brings a way of living within reach — and these fall in the direction opposite to occupation. The line is not whether there was arranging, but whether the space is larger or smaller afterwards. Appearance, reachability, expression, revision and bridging maintained or enlarged: releasing shaping. Pressed down out of reach: occupation. Showing you many things is not occupation; making you unable to see anything else is.

Filling does not require a single source. Many distributed sources can share one effective grammar of appraisal, with no coordination among them, and the effect is a candidate field with only that one scale left on it. The criterion asks how many effective grammars there are, not how many senders.

The two roads each have their own way of being occupied. The outside road can be filled with whole scripts, so that every candidate a man meets comes from one place; or it can be blocked, so that a class of candidates never reaches him. The endogenous road can be pressed shut, so that nothing surfaces from his own working. These must not be run together. The endogenous road pressed shut is the conditions of appearing being locked; it is not avowal being ghostwritten. A man who cannot get a candidate out of himself, and a man who is told what he cares about, are two things at two places — the first at appearance, the second at constitution.

9. Introjection

To judge whether an attribution is counterfeiting constitution, you do not first have to know whether first-person avowal occurred. The first person cannot be exhaustively verified from the third; the previous essay locked that down. There is another question you can ask: in this structure, on what does this content count as the bearer's?

There are two answers. Either the bearer claimed it, and that claiming stays where he can question it — the constituting work is being done by the first person. Or it was attributed to him, and the attribution is doing the constituting work. The second is introjection: the community's appraisal of a content, arranged as a value this bearer has claimed.

The criterion does not ask whether the attribution is true. An attribution can be perfectly right — the community says he values this, and he does. That changes nothing. Whether it or the bearer's own law is doing the constituting work, and whether it says something correct, are two questions. The criterion never needs to know whether avowal occurred, and never needs to know whether the attribution is true.

The signature judges a place, not an event. What is to be read is not whether the bearer raised a denial, but whether this structure has a place in which a denial could land as a denial. This matters for whether the criterion can be used at all: at the deepest reach of colonization the bearer raises no denial, because he has nothing to deny with. A signature keyed to the event of denial would never fire exactly where it is most needed. Whether the place exists is readable now.

The attribution need not be spoken by anyone. It can be carried by the relational structure. An arrangement that treats one metric as whether a person counts is issuing that attribution continuously without anyone opening their mouth, and a man's refusal of that metric has no form in which it could be recorded. An atmosphere no one is answerable for can do this, just as it can do locking.

The precise wording of the signature is the attribution's irrefutability, not its unwelcomeness. An attribution the bearer dislikes, even detests, but can contest, is not introjection. Contestable means the dispute has an outcome: his denial is recorded, answered, and may change the attribution's standing. Irrefutable means the denial has a destination arranged for it in advance — whatever he says gets rewritten into something else.

The signature has several common forms of differing purity. Dissent rewritten as betrayal or selfishness is one: a man's refusal of some collective goal is read, every time, as thinking too much of himself, and refusal can no longer exist as refusal. A purer form is denial pre-coded as lack of insight — a man's denial is counted as evidence for the attribution, so the more he denies it the more it is confirmed. At that point the place of rebuttal is not suppressed but abolished: any response can only prove the other side right.

That last form needs a line drawn around it. What falls under this judgment is not the assessment itself. A diagnosis, an evaluation, an outside description — so long as it leaves the bearer's places of refusal, review, second opinion and self-restatement standing, those places are open, however unwelcome or humiliating the assessment. What falls under this judgment is the step of pre-coding denial as symptom, because that is exactly what abolishes those places. It is the same shape as the previous essay's rule about locking: an offensive action is not a closing action; what is judged is whether the places are open, not how it felt.

10. Locking

Locking keeps the definition and threshold already established, and this essay only marks where it lands in colonization: the revisable place voided in advance within the relational structure. The threshold in its original form: some content-domain systematically excluded until the relevant candidates cannot enter the bearer's space of reflection, restatement and revision; or the bearer's refusal, reconstruction and revision in that domain pre-voided in the relational structure.

Three classes cannot be compressed into two. The previous essay established a threefold division: locking, releasing shaping, and non-shaping action that neither releases nor locks. Harmful does not equal locking. A narrowing, a pressure, an unpleasant action that does not reach the threshold falls into the third class and has its place there. This has to be held especially firmly here: the practical content of the criterion is narrow, not wide is more than half about not letting the third class be eaten.

Locking needs no actor. Even where no one reached in and touched a man's revisable place, that place can already have failed; an appraisal no one enforces, an atmosphere no one is answerable for, falls on the locking side.

What this essay borrows from locking is its criterion-form — a state threshold of the relational structure — not its slot on the previous essay's table of kinds of action. Run those together and you get the reading that colonization is a kind of action, and it is not.

Locking and introjection do not substitute for each other; what each seals is orthogonal to the other. Introjection strips the standing to deny: structurally a man may be free to speak, to say anything at all, and everything he says is rewritten into something else — the constituting work is thereby taken over. Locking seals the space to operate: the paths of reflection, restatement and revision are blocked outright, and whether he may speak is a separate matter. A content can be irrefutably attributed while the revisable place stays open; and a content the bearer avowed in his own law can afterwards have its revisable place voided from outside. The first is not locking. The second is not introjection. Each place is judged on its own, and that is the precondition for the three combining into a signature set at all.

11. Adjacent Forms, and Two Forkings

Three signatures complete, and the third person can determine external colonization in that domain. One missing and the set is incomplete — and the incomplete readings are asymmetric: attribution absent, this branch does not hold, determinately; attribution present with occupation or locking incomplete, the criterion stops at cannot-determine, and one does not conclude no from it.

Two incomplete forms sit closest to the boundary of the genus. The first is naked coercion: occupation and locking both present, no attribution. A man's candidate field is pressed very narrow, his refusal and withdrawal have nowhere to land, and no one has ever said this was his own value. The relation runs throughout as external requirement. The constitutive place is not counterfeited, so the genus does not hold. It can be harder to bear than many colonizations, and the criterion still does not change its verdict: how hard a thing is to bear is not the criterion; the state of the places is.

The second is a genuine avowal that has been locked. A content really was claimed by the bearer in his own law, and afterwards the revisable place was voided from outside. The constituting was made in his own law; no external end occupies that place; the genus does not hold. It is locking landing on an already-avowed content. The previous essay already judged it: at that point the content is no longer there in the manner of value-content, because revisability is written into constituting itself. Its gravity is not lessened by its not being called colonization.

What divides these two from introjection is whether an attribution is present and arranged as irrefutable. In a locked genuine avowal no one is telling the bearer this is your value; what is sealed is the revisable place, not the constitutive one. In introjection an attribution occupies the constitutive place and goes on looking like constituting.

One more form is often misread. A man lives by some set of requirements, and what holds that living in place is not any avowed content but the cost of departing. The requirements run throughout as external requirement and were never attributed as his value; only the cost of departure keeps him from departing. No attribution ever did constituting work in him. The genus does not hold; it falls on the locking side.

The criterion cuts two everyday categories in half. The first is rules. Rules cover every point of interaction, informal room for judgment disappears, occupation and locking are both present. Now look at the third: is there an attribution in place saying that following the procedure is his own value, and doing constituting work? If yes, three signatures, determinate reading. If no, that is going by the book — the constitutive place is not counterfeited, and it falls on the locking side.

The second is a narrative set hard. A story about who one is, treated as an unalterable frame of identity. If the story came from outside, is taken as constitution completed, and has nowhere to be revised, the three signatures are usually all present — an unalterable identity narrative by itself keeps other self-descriptions out, so occupation follows — and the reading is determinate. If it is the bearer's own narrative gone rigid, no external end occupies the constitutive place, and it does not fall under this judgment. It is the bearer voiding a still-applicable higher source of his own.

These forkings are not holes in the criterion. They are what happens where two indices cross. Classifying by the vehicle of intrusion and classifying by which place was violated are orthogonal axes. The names given by the first axis remain valid — each picks out a real form. What this essay supplies is the criterion those names need underneath them. One vehicle can carry two different place-states, and that is where the criterion forks.

12. Changing Is Not Being Colonized

Here is a general rule that blocks more misuse than the criterion itself. Revision and change are never evidence of colonization. They are evidence that the place is open.

A man's centre of value shifts, one devotion fades, another rises. These are mostly the dynamics of content, the ordinary business of a value-life and not a rare structural event. Reading he changed as a sign that he was colonized is reading the norm as pathology.

The rule has two qualifications. The first falls on self-colonization, and it is not an exception to the rule. The rule says change proves the place is open, and on that branch this stays true: the revisable place really is open there, and the bearer really is revising all along. What fails is the next step — inferring from an open place that the branch does not hold. That branch never rested on sealing a place. It rests on the standing stopping outside. So the place being open and the branch holding are two separate things.

So the qualification is content-specific, not candidate-field-specific: a man's candidate field can be wide, he can move freely among many candidates out of his own sources, while the standing of one particular content among them is carried, all along, from outside. Rewriting that one content, however many times, does not prove the standing has moved. And if it later does take a position under one of his own rows, what that shows is that the state has now changed — it does not prove in reverse that it was always his. This thread is available to the bearer only: self-colonization has no third-person criterion, so no one may turn a person's changing or not changing into a verdict about it.

The second qualification falls on time, by the same law. A successful revision proves that this place is open now, not that it was never sealed. That it can be changed later says the state no longer holds; it does not reach back and erase the reading at an earlier moment.

A word about the choice of three signatures. They are one cut this series takes, not the only possible cut. Drop any of them as a condition of determinate reading and you do not get a wider genus — the genus is still judged by the constitutive place. You get a wider use that this criterion cannot audit determinately. Those cuts are on record, and this essay does not call them wrong; it marks that it does not take them, and what taking them costs: once audit is loosened that far, ordinary upbringing, institutions and shared life are no longer distinguishable from colonization, and that is precisely why the word is worth using precisely.

13. The Upper Bound of Audit

Audit reads only whether the places are open or shut. It does not judge what the bearer really avows.

Three things can be asked, one per place. In this domain, can the bearer still get a candidate out of one of his own rows of source. For a given attribution, can his denial land as a denial. Are refusal, restatement, revision and withdrawal pre-voided in the relational structure. All three are facts about the relational structure, and the third person can read them.

The three readings are not of one kind. Three complete: the reading of external colonization in this domain is determinate. Denial able to land as denial: no irrefutable attribution is present, the external branch does not hold — a determinate negative. Attribution present with occupation or the revisable place incomplete: audit stops at cannot-determine. It can neither rule out that the attribution is only an echo of a real avowal, nor conclude no from that. Cannot-determine is itself a legitimate conclusion; it says the third person goes this far and no further. Treating incompleteness as a weaker positive, or as a negative, is reaching past what one can read.

Reaching past those three to read the first person is a different kind of overreach, and what makes it impossible is not modesty.

An audit that announces I can see what you really avow has put an attribution about the bearer in a position it cannot itself check: if he accepts, the conclusion stands; if he denies, the denial is read as further evidence for it. If such a conclusion also has no place for review, appeal and counter-audit, then what that relation structurally generates is exactly what introjection requires. This is not to say one sentence constitutes introjection — a single sentence is an event, introjection is a state of a place. It is to say that this kind of audit-relation tends to arrange attribution as irrefutable, and that is the very form it set out to audit.

So the upper bound of audit's authority and the criterion for introjection are two sides of one line. The bound is not an added modesty. It is a corollary of the criterion itself.

Audit's conclusions can therefore take only the form of places and signatures: this place is shut, that channel is open, this signature is absent, the three are not yet complete. They cannot take the form of the truth or falsity of content: this person's value-content is a forgery. That would require reading the first person.

This formal limit does not leave audit with nothing to say. It only fixes which kind of thing is sayable. Your denial has no place to land in this arrangement. This procedure leaves no channel for restatement, review and withdrawal. Every candidate that can enter this domain comes from one place. All of these name states of places, and all are sayable. What you really care about is not this — that is not sayable; it requires reading the first person. The line between sayable and unsayable falls there, not on how gently it is put.

14. Self-Colonization: What Is Missing Is Discovery

If a subject takes another's list of uses to claim its own value, its place of value-occurrence has already been occupied by that list, and thereafter, when it looks at itself, what it sees first is always the self that can be used. The prequel set that sentence down and left a question unanswered: how does such a list come to occupy that place, and what is the state once it has.

Self-colonization is this state: the bearer has performed the claiming of a content, while that content has never taken a candidate position under any of his own value-sources; the standing that makes it count as his value is carried by something outside his own sources. Such a claiming lands nowhere — and it is nonetheless taken as constitution completed, and maintained at the constitutive place.

To read this correctly you first have to see what is missing. What is missing is not permission at the level of type. For a bearer unfolded to 15DD, all four rows of value-source are present, and a new row does not replace an old one. Nearly any class of content can find a cell among those four at the level of type: that something is pleasant is an entirely permissible class of content on the row of the orientability of experience.

What is missing is discovery.

Knowing that such a value-representation exists, and discovering that you have this value, are two things. The first belongs to externally visible fact: some content is expressed, recognized, appraised or arranged as valuable by someone, and all of that can be observed without involving any row of your own. What is observable stops at representation: whether that content completed its first-person constituting in another bearer is not observable, since another's value cannot be read through. The second concerns this bearer: this content has taken a position under one of his own rows of source. The word that makes the difference is own.

Discovery here means only the second thing, not finding a fact that was already lying there. A content taking a position under a row of source means it has appeared, in this bearer's own working, as a candidate under that row — not that it has been verified as an existing item.

Two things are visible on this branch at once. Discovery has not held: the content never took a position under any row of his own. And something else stands in its place: an external warrant — something from outside his own sources holding up the standing of it counts. The warrant may be a reading issued by another's circuit of ends, an institutional arrangement, an authoritative pronouncement. The warrant is partly observable; whether discovery held is not.

Whether the warrant is true does not enter this judgment. It may be accurate: that value really does hold elsewhere, that pronouncement really is not false. It may be inaccurate: a misreading of another's ends, a formulation no one actually holds that keeps being copied, a representation that everyone values this. The criterion does not ask whether it is right. It asks whose sources carry the standing. This runs with the introjection rule, which likewise does not ask whether an attribution is true.

What is built between warrant and source has no fixed form. It can be inferential: since this value holds, I ought to have it too. It can be credential: another, or a third party, told me this, and I respond accordingly. It can be receiving an assigned place: they need me for this, so this is where my use lies. Form does not enter the judgment; the criterion asks only where the standing stops. Credence especially needs holding down: taking something on credit while the content also takes a position under one of your own rows is the ordinary way value occurs. Taking it on credit with the standing resting only on that pronouncement is what falls here. And ought to is this step's own tone of voice: whether there is a position under a row of source is not a matter of ought.

Two neighbours produce no position under a source either, and neither enters this judgment. Declaration does not produce one: I say this is my value, therefore it is — that step fails. Time does not produce one: I have held it long enough, surely it counts as mine by now — that step fails too. Both are blocked by the anti-subjectivist lock of the two previous essays, and there is no external end anywhere inside them, so by the definition of the genus they do not even enter it. They are simply failed claimings. The same place has two sides: that lock blocks a bearer from issuing himself a standing; this branch blocks something external from carrying it for him. Only the latter gives colonization, because only the latter has an external end present.

The seam was already left open in the previous essay. Appearance is a content's taking a candidate place in the bearer's field, and it does not ask where the content came from; what avowal requires is that the content has taken a candidate place within one of the bearer's value-source domains. Field and source-domain are not the same range, and the gap between them is where this branch lives. Discovery and appearance are therefore not the same thing: appearance is on the field, discovery is on the source-domain. Nor is this a new place added to the axis of occurrence. There is one candidate place, and a separate question of whether that candidate stands under one of the bearer's rows — and that question was already written into avowal's premise.

15. The Form on Each of the Four Rows

Each row has its own form. What the table records is not whose the content is, but whose sources carry the standing that makes the content count as mine. One and the same content can perfectly well take a position independently in two bearers; sharing a content has never been grounds for this judgment.

A list of uses is the most common form on the 14DD row. It is not the only one.

The 15DD row is structurally unlike the first three. Its content is the other to begin with, so the borrowing that goes wrong on the first three does not go wrong here on contact; it is the row least prone to error. What this row anchors is not the other's content of ends, but the other's standing as an end, and the fact that the first-person source of its value cannot be given, written or replaced by me.

Another's value cannot be read through. So what a bearer does on this row was never read correctly what the other wants; it is, under the condition of not being able to see through, forming a picture in his own law: it is an end, it wants this, my responding so means this. Only a bearer unfolded to this row has such a picture to make, and a picture is what it is — it can be made very well and it is still made under the condition of not seeing through.

Two things have to be kept apart here, or the line gets drawn wrong. One is what the other wants. That one the other decides: it occupies a first-person place on its own ends and bounds that no other can write for it, so its own account is an irreplaceable input to the picture. Listening to it is not outsourcing the picture — on the contrary, demoting the other's account uniformly to still has to be guessed independently by me is exactly taking over the other's first-person source, which this row expressly forbids. The other is how my responding so counts as my value. That one no one can do for me. The other can tell me what it wants; it cannot give me the standing by which my response counts.

So this row fails on the second of the two: the other's or a third party's requirement, approval or interpretation borrowed as the standing by which my response counts as my value, so that the bearer must obtain and therefore I count from an external circuit of ends. What the external warrant is holding up is not the content of the picture. It is the fact of its counting as my value.

Two things must therefore be written down. Listening to the other's account is not colonization; it is a first-person input no third-person material can replace. Behaviour, circumstance, history and what goes without saying remain legitimate material — especially where the other has not spoken, cannot speak, or the thing cannot be said, in which case the picture still has to be formed by the bearer himself. That material cannot override the other's own account, and cannot counterfeit the other's first-person source. Cannot be written by proxy is about a place; it does not say the other never misreads itself.

And guessing wrong is not colonization. The picture a bearer forms of another can be inaccurate; the revisable place is open, and he changes it next time. An inaccurate picture is still his own picture, just as a perfectly correct inference still produces no position under a source. What the criterion blocks was never accuracy. It is whose sources carry the standing.

This row can fail in two directions. One is the standing being carried from outside, which falls under this judgment. The other is presuming to have read the other through — taking one's own picture for the other's first person — which is performing introjection on the other. The line between them is that another's value cannot be exhaustively read, and the essay on the other raises it directly.

16. Three Borders, and What This Criterion Costs

The judgment has three borders, and cutting away any one of them wounds something that should not be cut.

The first separates it from 15DD's other-directed content. Cherishing someone's peace, cherishing a shared undertaking, cherishing care — these contents are full of the other, and really do require looking toward the other repeatedly, because the other is their object. The line is direction on the source-figure: on the 15DD row the bearer is the end that issues ends, and takes the other as an end; in the reading of uses the bearer is the end that gets used, and the other takes him as a means. Same matter, opposite directions, different cells. Read the direction; there is no need to imagine what would happen if the other were removed.

The second separates it from not-yet-rooted. A content has taken a position under a row of source, and this instance is new, not yet recurring through the bearer's working. That is ordinary value-occurrence, not pathology. Let the criterion eat this class and every new claiming becomes suspect — and the rule that change is evidence of an open place fails on the spot.

The third: not every failed claiming is self-colonization. Claimed, the second condition did not hold, and then it faded — that is only a failed claiming. This judgment requires that the second condition did not hold and that it is still being maintained at the constitutive place.

The criterion is narrow, and its cost is out in the open. An end that really did grow under the bearer's 14DD does not fall under this judgment even though someone else first pushed it at him, because provenance does not enter. A man whose whole operation hangs on others' appraisal does not fall under it either, so long as the content he values did take a position under one of his own rows. Self-colonization is not being deeply influenced. It is taking a cell on someone else's figure for one of your own. Many of the things ordinary language calls losing yourself do not fall on this branch. They have their own places.

17. It Can Only Be Read in Retrospect

A failed claiming and a completed one show no third-person-accessible surface difference on a single slice of running. The claiming place has taken its reading; the revisable place is open. The structural difference is there throughout — it just does not show a readable surface on any slice.

So the judgment on this branch lies wholly inside. The third person reads no surface on a slice, and what is readable requires following the bearer's own law, which no one can exhaustively read or write by proxy. There is no entrance here — not a temporary failure to see. On this branch audit cannot even reach cannot determine, which is at least an audit conclusion.

Nor can the judgment be contemporaneous. This branch requires the external warrant to be taken as constitution completed, and taken as contains within it that one has not, at this moment, seen it to be external. If a man sees in the moment that this is not something under his own sources, the taking-as fails on the spot and the state is dissolved. What can be seen through in the moment is already not the state this judgment names.

On this the two branches are exactly opposite, and the opposition follows directly from their two occupiers. In external colonization the bearer may know perfectly well that the attribution is foreign, and knowing does not dissolve it, because what is sealed is the revisable place. In self-colonization knowing dissolves it, because what is being held up from outside is precisely the standing — and once he sees it resting outside, his own law is already running that step.

So the only usable tense is retrospect. Afterwards, at a distance, the bearer asks again on what this content is his, and follows the account backwards: does the chain of standing finally stop at one of his own rows of source, or at an external warrant. This is not present-moment introspection. It is confronting yourself across time.

What is read is the landing point at that moment, not what came afterwards. The distinction matters, because results prove nothing here. A content later coming back from one of his own rows proves that by then it had taken a position — another event happened — and does not prove it was there originally. Conversely, its not coming back does not prove it never had a position: presence of a source and reachability of a source are two things, and not coming back may only mean reachability is still sealed. So whether recurrence happens is a thread, not a necessary and sufficient condition.

What retrospect reads is still structure, not feeling. That the judgment lies inside does not mean the inner self-report has the last word. A man feeling now that this is mine does not make it his; feeling that this is not mine dissolves no claiming. Nor is a later account automatically true: a person can write himself a clean story, and can also retroactively assign to the outside something that did grow under his own sources. The first person's privilege here is being able to follow his own law backwards. It is not that his self-report is final.

And there is no test. Anything that could be set out and followed from the outside proves something else: effort proves nothing, how much one draws on it proves nothing, what happens after the warrant is withdrawn proves nothing. What remains is the retrospect itself — the first person following the account backwards to see where the chain of standing stops. At one of his own rows, or at an external warrant. It is not a procedure. It is a tracing back.

18. Four Things to Hold, and Where the Way Out Is

One usable thread first: the provenance of recurrence. When a content fades and comes back, does it come back as a candidate under one of his own rows, or does it need a fresh external warrant to come back at all. This thread is available to the bearer only.

And one thing to get exactly right, or this judgment reads like an online machine. What is claimed is a structural dependency, not any ongoing act of drawing on something. An external warrant can be remembered, made into a habit, and thereafter recur automatically, needing no external input in reality and running no explicit inference. That does not change the judgment: the source is still outside; the running need not be. Automatic, effortless, long-standing — none of the three moves where the chain of standing lands.

Time does not move it either. However long a content is held, the standing does not thereby migrate from outside to under his own sources, because repeated claiming produces no source. So this is not something that settles itself with time: if that content finally does land under one of his rows in his working, another event has happened; this one did not accumulate to a threshold.

Four things then have to be held. First, standing is not cost. What one pays for a value can be enormous: a man who genuinely cherishes caring for his family pays hugely, and that is cost in action, unrelated to this judgment. What is at issue is what carries the standing by which the content counts as his. The cost can be very high and the standing never once have stopped outside.

Second, effortfulness is not the criterion. An external warrant may be continuously present and very easy to draw on; it may long since have become a habit and need no drawing on at all. Effortlessness does not prove the state does not hold, and effort does not prove it does. What is readable is where the chain of standing lands, not how easy the drawing is.

Third, no one else can issue this reading. That is not a prohibition but an impossibility: reading it requires following the bearer's own law. A man who says this was never really yours has not determined self-colonization; he cannot. What he has done is something else — handing down an attribution the bearer cannot check, which is exactly the relational structure external colonization requires. The two branches lock together here.

Fourth, doubt does not dissolve a claiming — least of all present doubt, since contemporaneous judgeability and this state are mutually exclusive. A moment's wavering neither establishes the judgment nor dissolves any claiming. What has to move is the landing point read in retrospect, not that one flicker of feeling.

The way out is now fixed, and it is not the same as knowing dissolves it. Dissolving means the state no longer holds: once he sees the standing propped from outside, that content falls back to being a candidate and is no longer taken as constitution completed. Whether it then becomes his value is a further step, requiring it to take a position under one of his own rows. Dissolving does nothing for that step. It only clears the seat.

And the way out falls on that second step. Since every self-questioning proceeds under the same warrant, the exit is not on the side of self-questioning; nor is it on the auditor's side, for the reason just given. The way out is to give that content a chance to take a position under one of the bearer's own rows, or to let a candidate not generated by that warrant take a position. Such a candidate can come from an outside vantage that is heterogeneous, or from the endogenous road. And everything after a candidate takes its position stays, entirely, with the bearer.

19. Pre-occupation at Subjects-to-Be

In a content-domain where first-person avowal has not yet come to run of itself, external colonization takes another form: pre-occupation. It stays on the external branch and the criterion is unchanged; only the landing point of each of the three actions moves with the state of that place.

Introjection here is not displacing a first-person place that already exists. Subject-place recognition presupposes an avowal already made, and in a domain not yet running of itself no such recognition is even defined. What an attribution issued here does is take a determinate content as a completed constituting that never had a chance to happen. Locking here falls on the pre-voiding of the future revisable place: an arrangement makes some content, by the time that door comes to run, already unrestatable and unrevisable. The three together point at a place not yet running, so that it is already filled the moment it begins to run.

The judgment goes by domain, not by whole subject. The same subject-to-be is judged as a complete subject in domains already running of themselves, and by pre-occupation in domains not yet running. Maturity never arrives in one block.

How a future revisable place is pre-voided in the present has three signals readable now. Is there an arrangement to hand over interpretive authority as the first-person place matures, or is that content's interpretation arranged to belong permanently to the outside. Can the subject-to-be's emerging refusals, deviations and reconstructions really change the arrangement, or are they read, without exception, as not yet understanding. Is the present configuration marked as a revisable present arrangement, or as a future irrefutable final content. All three are present facts about the relational structure, and they turn the future revisable place from a conjecture into a reading.

It follows that in domains where the first-person place is not yet running of itself, self-colonization is undefined. That judgment requires the bearer to have performed a claiming, and with the door not yet running there is nothing to perform it with. In those domains a subject-to-be can only be pre-occupied.

The vagueness here falls on typing, not on the criterion. A content taken at first as one's own value and later not — that movement needs no adjudication: the criterion asks whether future revisability was pre-voided, and that is a relational fact readable now. As for the later change itself, it shows the place is open now, i.e. that pre-occupation no longer holds; by the qualification on time, it does not reach back and erase the earlier reading. In a subject-to-be this movement is normal maturing; in a complete subject it is a discovery in the course of running. Same shape, different circumstances.

And there is a line here. A guardianship network maintaining the reachability of candidates, maintaining expression, maintaining future revisability is not colonization. Fixing any candidate configuration as a completed first-person value-content is. The difference between maintaining and fixing is what this whole judgment hangs on. A guardianship network can arrange a great deal of what a subject-to-be meets, can choose what to teach and what to teach first, and none of that brings it under this judgment. What brings it under is sealing one content's place before that door comes to run.

Pre-occupation is a violation not because this subject-to-be will one day be a complete subject. It is already a bearer of end-value, and that not-yet-running place is already its own. What is violated is not a future entitlement; it is a place that belongs to it now. How a guardian ought to act, and what obligations follow, this essay does not judge. That is the business of the critique of practice.

20. The Places Never Change Hands

Colonization acts always on reachability, never on presence. The form holds at two levels at once.

At the level of the source: a source's presence cannot be destroyed by colonization. What can be occupied, blocked, sealed is a source's reachability, its paths of appearing, the concrete contents it yields. A man's row of value-source can go a long time yielding nothing that enters the candidate field, and the row is still there.

At the level of the places: claiming, revision and withdrawal are structurally permanent. What colonization can do is make them unreachable in running.

The two are not merely similar in shape. Both are one modal fact showing twice: what is constitutive cannot be abolished by a relational act. Attribution, appraisal, arrangement, pressure — all of these are acts within relations; sources and places are not given by relations, they are the bearer's own constitution as a bearer of end-value. Relational things can seal the road to them. They cannot take them away.

What is permanent is the belonging of the place; its running form may be not yet generated, already self-running, or temporarily unreachable. For a complete subject and for domains already running, the place is in operation and can be sealed unreachable. For a subject-to-be's domains not yet running, the belonging and the reservation of the place are already its own while the running form is not yet generated — and what pre-occupation violates is precisely the openness of that reservation to future operation.

From which one sentence follows: complete colonization is not a subject's ceding. What can really be ceded is not called colonization; it is called replacement. The cell of door present, unused is where this criterion is registered: a man can wholly stop using that place in running, and his standing as a bearer is not lost. Disuse is a matter of running; ceding would be a matter of standing, and the latter is impossible. That cell names a place's running form and carries no implication that the bearer brought it about: a man who no longer uses that place himself, and a man arranged out of reach of it, share the cell.

Recoverability follows too, with a limit. That the place was not transferred does not mean recovery is always practically possible. Permanence guarantees that recovery still has a target belonging to the bearer; it does not guarantee the target can always be reached under actual conditions. How reachability is actually restored in time is the business of the essay on dynamics.

21. Colonization Takes Two Subjects

The original solitary subject cannot be colonized. Each branch has its own reason, and the two reasons are independent.

The external branch requires an attribution, and attribution is material of the social-recognition kind, which takes at least two subjects to be defined at all. The self branch requires an external warrant entering the bearer's chain of standing, and a warrant must have an external end behind it, or the trace one left in institutions and history — likewise at least two subjects. Each road independently requires a second subject, so the genus as a whole does not hold.

The self branch does not require that the content really has become a value on another subject's source-figure. Whether the warrant is true does not enter the judgment; all that is needed here is that it have an external provenance.

The solitary subject meant here is the prequel's thought-experiment one: a subject that never had a second subject or any social history. The condition is not read as a head-count at a moment. A subject that once formed a list in society and later lived alone, or became the last one left, can still carry the state formed earlier; that is no counter-example, because the second subject colonization requires is a relational or historical provenance, not a person present now.

The column of modality asks one thing only: does the second subject constitute the first subject's end-value. Price constitutes, because the price of a thing just is given by a relation between at least two parties. Resonance does not: the structure that resonates is already complete in a solitary subject, and the second subject only makes it occur. Colonization shares the cell with resonance — here the second subject supplies material, while the state holds at the first subject's place, and it constitutes not one part in any degree of the first subject's end-value. Sharing a cell is not sharing a type: the material of an external end really is a necessary relational component of this state's holding, whereas what resonates is complete without waiting on a second subject.

So the prequel's sentence gets an exact reading: a subject's standing as an end holds up in a solitary universe, because its footing never depended on a buyer for its uses. No buyer, no price, and no colonization — and value all the same.

The solitary subject's value can change, and having changed it is still its own. One content fades, one comes back from the edge to the centre, one returns after a while. These are the dynamics of content, aimed at no particular dimension, the ordinary business of a value-life. The material both branches require is absent, so those movements can only be its own.

It is not free of pathology, though. A bearer voiding a higher source whose conditions of application have actually arrived — that is the active closing marked out earlier. It is not colonization, because there is no external end and no second subject. There is more than one way for value to go wrong, and colonization is only the one that takes a second subject. Which is exactly why the word should not be used as a general name for value going wrong.

22. Layering: Severing, Cultivation, Misclaim

Colonization and the severing judged by power theory do genuinely overlap in one place. Severing's locking has four layers, and the layer of interpretation — the receiving end interpreting the return-flow as its own growth, its own choice, its own reason — is exactly where both hold at once: the right to interrupt is cancelled, and an attribution occupies the constitutive place.

Overlap is not mutual reducibility, for three reasons. First, the predicate severing is relational. It says the receiving end's law has lost its right to interrupt within this relation; without an acting end the sentence has no subject. Colonization's predicate falls at the bearer's own place, where a second subject supplies material and is not the subject of the sentence. Second, the objects differ: severing's object is the right to interrupt; colonization's object is the constitutive place of value. A man can wholly lose the right to interrupt within a relation while no attribution has occupied his constitutive place; and he can, inside a relation that does not cancel his right to interrupt, have that place occupied by an irrefutable attribution. Third, severing can run throughout as external requirement; external colonization additionally requires an attribution of his own value occupying the constitutive place. Whether it is done openly does not enter: an external colonization can perfectly well announce this is your real value and read your denial as you have not yet understood yourself.

And self-colonization does not require a currently identifiable acting end. It can perfectly well be the running state left behind by an earlier severing, and that does not change its judgment now: as a state, it does not fall under severing.

Cultivation is not on the same layer either, and here a tempting pairing has to be corrected. The opposite of cultivation is not colonization. It is locking — the kind with a receiving end, which is severing. External colonization's complete signature includes locking, and additionally requires occupation of the candidate field and an irrefutable attribution; self-colonization is not judged along the locking–release axis at all. The earlier image of loosening the grid and sealing the grid can stand, read precisely: the places cultivation maintains are exactly the places colonization seals, one by one.

The structural reason the two are not on one layer is that their predicates have different subjects. At the layer of criterion they are already unified: cultivation and colonization are both judged by structural effect, and neither asks after intent. What differs is that cultivation predicates an action and colonization predicates a state. Within one and the same episode, this action is cultivation and this content's state is self-colonization can both be true without contradiction.

From which a boundary follows, and it is not a special exemption but a direct corollary of the different subjects: an incomplete cultivation is not colonization. An actor opens every place, hands judgment back, and the content in the end connects to none of the bearer's rows of source. He has colonized no one. That the second root did not grow does not reach back and change the character of the first. Without this line, every teaching that failed to take would be retroactively called colonization — precisely what a narrow criterion is for.

What the second root is can now be said, on one of the two branches. Cultivation is complete only when the receiving end's own step actually occurs, and that step has two branches: if the outcome falls on a particular content's occurrence, the step is first-person avowal; if it falls on structural dimension-opening, the step is the taking-up of valuing. On the content branch a further layer is needed, because there the previous essay already had two steps: the content taking a position under one of the bearer's own rows is the premise on which first-person avowal can be completed, and the second root itself is still the avowal. Premise missing, avowal cannot complete, and the second root does not grow. On the dimension-opening branch there is no such layer, since there is no particular content for this criterion to work on.

So three things adjoin here without being equated: taking a position under a row of source is the premise, first-person avowal is the second root itself, and self-colonization is a claiming still maintained as completed while the premise is missing. The second root not growing says only that either the premise or the avowal did not happen; self-colonization additionally requires the claiming to be maintained at the constitutive place. A content that took no position and then faded is only a failed claiming.

Three things must be held here or this layer slides into a ruler of results. Whether an act was release-ward or closure-ward is determinable at the time, by its structural effect on the bearer's places; this judgment cannot be deferred, since deferring it means using results as the criterion. What was undetermined at the time is only whether the second root would grow, and that was never in the actor's hands — its being undetermined is not a defect in the criterion but the structure of the thing. And impeded development is not a criterion: by it, a true cultivation that happened to bring no visible progress would be retroactively called colonization, and a colonization that happened to accompany considerable achievement would escape judgment. A criterion of places does not look at output.

Cultivation has one more layer here, where it meets the 15DD row, and it adds no new condition — it is a direct reading of what the previous essay established: the actor holds no constituting share in the receiving end's first-person completion. To open some receiving end's space of occurrence, an actor has to make some judgment about that receiving end; another's value cannot be read through, so the judgment is only ever a picture formed in his own law. The picture may be accurate or not, and that is not the difference. The difference is what he takes the picture to be: taken as his own judgment on which to clear a road, the receiving end's share stays in the receiving end's hands; handed down as the other's completed self-knowledge, he is claiming to hold the other's share — and by cultivation's own condition, that is no longer cultivation. This distinction, keeping versus filling in, and the guardianship distinction, maintaining versus fixing, are one line appearing twice.

Last, the same-form relation with misclaim. This framework established elsewhere a more general form: a construct that presents a credential of standing it has not earned is judged as showing more than holding; the judgment is retrospective, does not ask after motive, and its remedy is reckoning and being questioned. Introjection is exactly how that form falls in the field of value-occurrence: what is grantable and revocable has no constituting power, and the constitutive credential social recognition presents here is precisely the one it does not hold.

External colonization has two things more than a simple misclaim. The misclaim has already taken up the constitutive reading within the bearer's own architecture of occurrence — not merely that the outside presents it so, but that the reading on the bearer's side is occupied as well; a structural matter, not the bearer's subjective assent. And the channel of reckoning for that attribution has been sealed: his denial cannot be registered as a denial of it. What is sealed is the channel of rebuttal for that one attribution, not the whole of his paths of reflection, restatement, revision and withdrawal, which is what locking judges. A misclaim can occur with the channel open and be corrected there; colonization is the state in which that channel is sealed.

The self branch is likewise, in form, showing more than holding: what the external warrant actually holds is at most an external requirement, a position of authority, an institutional reading, or a circular formulation; what it presents is that this content has already taken a position under one of the bearer's own rows. Whether the warrant is itself true changes nothing — either way it does not hold the latter credential. But this gives the branch no third-person criterion. To determine that showing exceeds holding here you would have to know the content is not given by the bearer's sources, and that requires reading his own law. The upper bound is one and the same on both branches, and the sameness is worth recording: a general form can hold equally on both while the reach of the criterion does not widen.

The two are not mutually reducible. This essay's criterion is established independently from the modal asymmetry of the three places, not derived from the general form; this only records the relation, and does not define colonization as a species of misclaim. One further sentence comes out of the relation: self-questioning cannot guarantee against all of one's own blind spots — that is what the general judgment established — and the structural reason self-colonization is hard to read from inside is the same, namely that every self-questioning proceeds under the same warrant, and a single slice offers no structural difference to tell them apart.

23. What Remains

After an external end occupies the places of occurrence, how a source's reachability changes, how the dominant centre of gravity shifts, why a content fades at this moment and returns at that one — those belong to the essay on dynamics. One thing there joins directly onto this essay: colonization does not change the presence of a source; what it locks is the source's reachability and the paths of occurrence. This essay gives the structure of that lock. It does not write how it loosens in time.

What to do when one bearer's several avowed contents demand incompatible actions belongs to the essay on conflict. Unranked in being and decided in practice do not conflict.

Why another's value cannot be exhaustively read, cannot be compared by an outside ruler, cannot be unified, belongs to the essay on the other. The upper bound both branches share — the boundary of the third-person criterion's domain of definition — is that epistemic limit showing itself on the pathology side. The two point at one place, and that essay raises it directly.

This essay gives criteria and readings of places. It gives no normative force. Whether a colonization that holds ought to be dissolved, who is fit to conduct an audit, what obligations a guardianship network bears at a subject-to-be — each has its place, and this essay marks the address and stops. They belong to the critique of practice.

The three places are modally different, so an outside action gets a determinate reading from which one it lands on. The place of appearance can be occupied. The constitutive place can be occupied by an irrefutable attribution, or maintained as constitution completed by an external warrant. The revisable place can be voided in advance. All of this happens at one and the same set of places, and that set has never changed hands. Colonization has never actually constituted anything, and never actually taken anything away. Everything it can do falls on the side of reachability. The places of claiming, revision and withdrawal are the bearer's own, throughout.
